title: Prompt chunking and stitching protocol notes
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, implementable protocol for client-side prompt chunking and server-side stitching to support very long context prompts while preserving low tail latency and cost-awareness. This is a personal scratchpad — not final.

Problem summary:
- Customers want to submit extremely long prompts (multi-MB) composed of document attachments, long context windows, or conversation histories. Sending full context to the runtime for every request is expensive and latency-heavy.
- Need a way for clients to split (chunk) input, send incremental pieces, let server index / cache partial results (KV/embeddings/prefix cache), and then stitch an assembled reasoning pass without re-running expensive sections.
- Also must support streaming generation to clients that expect tokens as they are produced.

Goals:
- Minimize repeated compute across requests by letting server cache chunk encodings and reuse them across sessions/requests where appropriate.
- Keep API simple for clients (fallback to single-call full-input mode optional).
- Provide deterministic stitching semantics so outputs are reproducible and traceable.
- Have opt-in privacy controls (client marks chunk as ephemeral or private, controlling caching/retention).
- Graceful failure and partial-result delivery when chunks fail to upload or expire.

High-level flow (ideas):
1) Client splits large prompt into ordered chunks (size heuristics: ~16k tokens or based on logical boundaries like paragraphs).
2) For each chunk, client computes an optional lightweight fingerprint (sha256), and calls /chunks/upload (multipart friendly) with metadata.
3) Server responds with chunk_id (CID) and whether a cache hit (already present) or stored.
4) When all chunks are registered, client does a /generate request with an ordered list of chunk_ids plus generation parameters.
5) Server fetches chunk encodings (from cache or on-demand encoders), composes a stitched prefix (concatenate KV caches / embeddings / tiled attention state as supported), then runs decode. Streaming tokens are emitted incrementally to client.

API shape (draft):
- POST /chunks/upload
  body: {
    "session_id": "string",
    "chunk_index": 0,
    "fingerprint": "sha256",
    "flags": ["cacheable" | "private" | "ephemeral"],
    "content_type": "text/plain|json|html",
    "content": "base64 or text (small chunks only)"
  }
  response: { "chunk_id": "cid:xxxx", "stored": true|false, "encoder_hint": "qlora-v2" }

- POST /generate
  body: {
    "session_id": "string",
    "chunk_ids": ["cid:1", "cid:2", ...],
    "stitch_strategy": "concatenate|sliding-window|summary-rewrite",
    "stream": true|false,
    "decode_params": { "max_tokens": 512, "temp": 0.2 }
  }
  response: stream of token events or final json {"task_id": "t123", "status":"ok"}

Server-side stitch strategies (notes):
- concatenate: naive join; simplest, minimal server work. Works for models with huge context windows or when chunks are encoded as KV cache segments.
- sliding-window: keep a moving window of last N tokens across chunk boundaries (useful for autoregressive LM that cannot accept arbitrarily long concatenated KV). Requires re-encoding overlapping borders or using summary vectors.
- summary-rewrite: server constructs short summaries for older chunks and uses those as compressed context. Summaries themselves are cached and versioned.

Caching model: chunk_id -> {
  "encoder_version": "v1.1",
  "kv_shards": ["shardA","shardB"],
  "summary": "optional",
  "last_access": "ts",
  "policy": "retain|evict"
}

Stitching implementation notes:
- Ideally chunk upload triggers server-side encoding to a KV segment (async) so subsequent generate calls are fast.
- Where feasible, use continuous prefix cache: an ordered set of KV blobs that can be concatenated with minimal recompute.
- For models/hardware that don't support concatenated KV natively, provide a fallback: re-encode boundary tokens with overlap of X tokens (configurable) then decode over the overlapped window and stitch outputs deterministically.
- Keep sequence position offsets per chunk to allow token-level provenance (which chunk produced/affected token). Useful for traceability and evaluation.

Streaming model & partial results:
- If stream=true on /generate: server should emit tokens as produced, and also periodically emit "progress" events (percent chunks encoded/loaded).
- For long tail where some chunks are still being encoded, send partial answer based on currently available context and include a metadata flag "partial=true". Client can opt to wait for final stitching by passing wait_for_complete=true.

Error cases & semantics:
- Missing chunk_id: respond 400 with list of missing chunk_ids and a suggested corrective action (re-upload or fail).
- Chunk expired between upload and generate: server returns status=partial with which chunks were present. If client opted for strict=true, server returns error and no output.
- Fingerprint mismatch on re-upload: server returns conflict (409) and existing chunk_id; allow override with force=true.

Privacy & retention:
- Flags at upload time control retention and caching. Default policy: cacheable for 7 days, private for 24 hours. Allow org-level overrides.
- Ephemeral chunks: never written to durable store, kept in memory until session ends.

Config knobs (per-session or per-route):
- chunk_max_tokens: int
- chunk_overlap_tokens: int (when using overlap fallback)
- max_cached_chunks_per_session
- summary_threshold_tokens: when to auto-generate summaries
- encode_async: true|false (if true, generate will wait for encoding or use partial semantics)

Performance tradeoffs:
- Asynchronous encoding: lowers request latency for initial uploads, but increases complexity for consistency and partial responses.
- Eager encoding: upload latency higher but generate is fast and deterministic.
- Sliding-window overlap reduces cache reuse but works on HW/models without native KV stitching.

ASCII flow (quick sketch):

Client                       Server
  | -- upload chunk 0 ----->  | accept -> encode async -> store CID
  | -- upload chunk 1 ----->  | accept -> cache hit? -> store
  | -- /generate with CIDs -> | fetch KV segments -> stitch -> decode -> stream tokens -> |
  | <--- token stream ------- |

State diagram (very rough):
- chunk: uploaded -> encoding_pending -> encoded -> cached -> evicted
- generate: submitted -> gathering_context -> decoding -> completed | failed

Open questions / TODOs:
- Encoding fingerprint format: do we include tokenizer + special tokens + encoder hyperparams in the hash? (Yes: must include encoder_version)
- TTL policy defaults: discuss with privacy & legal.
- Backwards compatibility: how to support clients that can't chunk? Keep generate accept raw text as before.
- Metric surfaces: need chunk-level hit-rate, average encode latency, and cost-savings per route.
- Storage format: compressed KV blobs vs per-layer shard references; what exposes least coupling to model internals?

Example end-to-end sketch (pseudo):
- client: split into 3 chunks -> upload each
- server: returns CID_a, CID_b, CID_c. CID_a encoded and cached. CID_b in queue, CID_c cache-hit.
- client: POST /generate {chunk_ids:[CID_a,CID_b,CID_c], stitch_strategy:"concatenate", wait_for_complete:false}
- server: uses available encoded KV for a and c, starts to decode with best-effort; emits tokens with partial=true
- after b finishes encoding, server emits finalization event and optionally a retraction/patch if final output changes materially (or returns final_result task_id to fetch later)

Patch model (optional): to avoid retractions, support a "stable_output_at_offset": client can request only tokens after chunk B encoded; or server returns "patches" that apply diffs to previously streamed tokens (hard for clients; prefer simple: partial + final state).

Notes to self:
- Prototype: implement upload endpoint, simple encode-to-kv, naive concatenate stitch. Bench with Llama2-13B quantized path on a single A100 GPU.
- Instrument: tag any generation request with chunk provenance for debug and quality evals.

References / related docs (internal):
- ENG-1427 (chunking infra spike)
- runtime/pull/890 (initial chunk cache implementation PR)

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after chat with Priya on 2025-03-04.
